real_qa.q: What is the typical ROI timeline for CMP Efficiency Solutions water efficiency valves on commercial properties?
real_qa.r: Our target is really a 12 month or less ROI. Now, that metric all depends on the size of your water meter and, of course, how much water you're using. But we like to see, you know, 12 months, not longer, not usually longer than two years.

real_qa.q: How does CMP Efficiency Solutions analyze water consumption savings differently across hospitality, food manufacturing, and other verticals?
real_qa.r: Every vertical has its own metric by what you measure the success of the product at. For a car wash, it's how much water are you spending per car. At a hotel, it's how much water are you spending on water per door night. When we're doing our analysis, we're really looking at 12 months worth of bills and want to know an exact comparison to before the valve and after the valve.
real_qa.requete: water consumption metrics by industry vertical

real_qa.q: What valve sizes does CMP Efficiency Solutions offer for commercial applications like hotels, car washes, and breweries?
real_qa.r: Standard valve sizes start at a half an inch, three quarters of an inch, mostly for residential. On the commercial side, you'll start seeing some at one inch. The most common size is a two inch, which would cover most car washes, hotels, senior living, multifamily. For food and beverage manufacturing and golf courses and irrigation, the size of the valves go up—we've seen orders with 8-inch, 10-inch, and 12-inch valves.

real_qa.q: What does CMP Efficiency Solutions offer in its free trial program to help potential clients verify water savings claims?
real_qa.r: We do a free 90-day trial. We'll send you five valves, install them for 90 days, and after that, buy them or send them back. I wouldn't send out $25,000 worth of valves unless I was 100% sure that the client's going to keep them.
